title: Unicode and International Text
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of unicode and international text and identify when it is appropriate in a Java program.
Apply at least one of the lesson topics—utf-16 code units—in a small, readable example.
Predict the example result and check it against the stated output or a boundary-case test.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study unicode and international text with a short explanation, an original visual map, a Java example, and a check you can perform yourself. Focus on the relationship between the rule and the behavior rather than memorizing isolated syntax.
content.why_it_matters: This concept matters because it helps you process text correctly while accounting for immutability, equality, and Unicode. In this lesson, focus on utf-16 code units and use a minimal example to check what the rule actually guarantees.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: String values are immutable, so methods return new results rather than changing existing text. Compare contents with `equals`, and distinguish UTF-16 code units from Unicode code points and visible graphemes. Apply that reasoning specifically to utf-16 code units and confirm the result with the example or a targeted test. The important habit is to make the assumptions explicit and use the code example as a small experiment.
